mechanics.name: Hope
mechanics.currentEffect: Once the Exit Gates are powered, Hope activates and grants you 3/4/5% Haste for the remainder of the Trial.
activation: The Exit Gates must be powered.
Ends/deactivates when: The effect ends when the Trial ends.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.2.0): Reduced Haste from 5/6/7% to 3/4/5%; current duration remains the remainder of the Trial.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: When the Exit Gates are powered, you move faster until the Trial ends.
duration: Remainder of the Trial after the Exit Gates are powered.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: Activates once when the Exit Gates are powered and remains active for the rest of the Trial.

editorial.summary: Once the Exit Gates are powered, gain permanent 5% Haste for the rest of the Trial.
useCases: Turn an endgame chase into a much harder catch for standard-speed Killers.
Reach gates, teammates, and rescue positions faster after the generators are completed.
Stack with strong chase fundamentals to convert a narrow endgame lead into an escape.
counters: Provides absolutely no value before the Exit Gates are powered.
A match that collapses before endgame leaves the perk completely dead.
Some Killer powers can still ignore or overwhelm the 5% movement advantage.
Hex: Under Your Thumb can cap running Haste while the Hex remains lit.
pros: Permanent endgame Haste with no cooldown once activated.
Affects every movement decision after generators are complete, not just one chase.
Can be extremely difficult for basic-attack Killers to overcome in good Survivor hands.
cons: Dead perk slot for most of the Trial.
Requires the team to reach powered gates before any value appears.
analysis: Hope takes this position because 5% permanent Haste is a genuinely powerful effect attached to one of the harshest activation conditions in the game: the team must already have powered the Exit Gates. Before that moment, Hope is not conditional value or reduced value; it is no value at all.

Once active, however, the effect is extremely clean. Movement speed affects every loop, transition, gate rotation, rescue approach, and attempt to reach safety. Against ordinary 115% movement-speed Killers, a strong looper can convert a 5% increase into significantly longer endgame chases because the Killer gains distance more slowly around every structure.

The perk also pairs naturally with Adrenaline. One provides the immediate health-state and burst transition when generators finish; the other stays active for the entire endgame afterward. Coordinated teams can exploit that combination to turn the final generator into a major tempo swing.

Hope has an important consistency limitation because Survivor loadouts need to help the team reach endgame in the first place. A slot that is dead during a losing match can contribute to the reason that match never stabilizes. Hope is therefore a powerful closer rather than a universally strong opener or midgame tool.
editorial.verdict: An elite endgame closer held back by doing nothing before the gates are powered. If your team reaches the final phase, permanent 5% Haste can make the Killer's last chase dramatically harder.
